**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding**: no standardised intake (fitness assessment, goal-setting, payment setup, community integration). Critical for Day 1–30 retention and baseline outcomes tracking.
- **Cancellation & churn**: no documented exit interview, win-back protocol, or pause-to-reactivation workflow. You're losing data on *why* members leave.
- **Class quality audit**: no mechanism to audit coaching consistency, form cuing, energy, music/pacing. Quality decay is silent.
- **Member check-ins & milestone tracking**: no scheduled touchpoint cadence (30/60/90 day) or how to celebrate/retain via progress visibility.
- **Health & safety incident reporting**: no template for injuries, complaints, near-misses, or escalation path—legal/insurance risk.
- **Referral programme**: no mechanics, incentive structure, or tracking SOP. Low-hanging growth lever.
- **GDPR & member data privacy**: no consent logging, data retention, or breach protocol—compliance liability.
- **Supplies & sundries ordering**: no stock thresholds, vendor management, or delivery SOP (towels, cleaning, equipment repairs).

**Needs updating**

- **Coach onboarding (Coaches)**: likely missing probation KPIs, shadowing structure, or competency sign-off before solo teaching.
- **Retention/engagement (Clients)**: no defined win-back sequence for lapsed members or pause-to-resume workflow.
- **Complaints handling**: assume missing escalation path, response time SLA, and documentation for pattern spotting.
- **Marketing campaign execution**: no post-campaign member journey SOP (how leads become trials, trials become paying members).
- **Financial controls**: no invoice approval, refund authority, or reconciliation checklist (especially relevant for memberships/packages).

# Execution Plan: Service Menu Build for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality TODAY** — Pull your last 3 months of bookings/invoices. Map every service you've actually sold (classes, PT, challenges, memberships, add-ons). This is your baseline, not aspirational. Ignore what you *think* you offer; build from what's generating income.

• **Create TWO separate docs, not one** — Coaches need: pricing, commission structure, what they can/can't promise, upsell sequences, package boundaries (e.g., "PT includes THIS many form checks, NOT nutrition planning"). Members need: clean pricing, what's included per tier, what costs extra, and friction-free upgrade paths. Different audiences, different info.

• **Price-anchor to your best performer** — Identify your highest-margin OR highest-volume service. Lock that price first. Build everything else relative to it (e.g., if group classes hit £12/drop-in, PT becomes 4-6x that). This prevents pricing chaos and gives coaches a clear hierarchy to sell from.

• **Make it a 1-page visual for coaches** — They won't memorize a document. Use a simple table: Service | Duration | Price | Commission | What's Included | Upsell Trigger. Post it in the staff area. Update quarterly, not continuously.

• **Test pricing with 3-5 existing members first** — Show them the menu before launch. "Would you upgrade to this if it was £X?" Catches blind spots before coaches start selling the wrong value prop.

**Deadline: 1 week. Ship it rough; iterate after feedback.**
